question.problem:
Find a Cartesian equation of the plane that passes through the point $P(0,0,3)$ and is perpendicular to the line 
${\begin{aligned}x=2+2t \\ y=5t \\ z=1-t\end{aligned}.$
question.worked_solution:
First, we note that the position vector of $P$ is $p=⟨0,0,3⟩.$ From the parametrical equation, we find that the line is parallel to the vector $⟨2,5,-1⟩.$ So, the normal vector of the plane is 

$$
n=⟨2,5,-1⟩.
$$

Using the dot product, we can find the equation of the plane as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}(r-p)\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n & =p\cdot n \\ r\cdot ⟨2,5,-1⟩ & =⟨0,0,3⟩\cdot ⟨2,5,-1⟩ \\ r\cdot ⟨2,5,-1⟩ & =-3.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to obtain the Cartesian equation of the plane, we substitute $r=⟨x,y,z⟩$ into the equation above. Hence,

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨x,y,z⟩\cdot ⟨2,5,-1⟩ & =-3 \\ 2x+5y-z & =-3 \\ 2x+5y-z+3 & =0.\end{aligned}
$$
